cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is an evolved lightweight LLM coordinator?
cards.answer: A compact model (roughly 0.6B parameters plus a ~10K-parameter head), optimized with an evolutionary strategy, that delegates work across a pool of larger LLMs by assigning roles like Thinker, Worker, or Verifier at each turn.

cards.heading: Coordination vs weight merging
cards.question: Why does this coordination approach work where weight merging cannot?
cards.answer: Coordination only needs each model's inputs and outputs, so it works across mismatched architectures and closed/proprietary APIs that weight merging can't touch.

cards.heading: Why the coordinator stays tiny
cards.question: Why does the coordinator only need to be sub-1B parameters when the worker models are much larger?
cards.answer: Competence stays in the worker LLMs; the coordinator only has to learn who should play which role when, not perform the tasks itself.

cards.heading: Optimization method finding
cards.question: What optimization method beat RL, imitation learning, and random search for training this coordinator, and under what conditions?
cards.answer: Separable CMA-ES (an evolutionary strategy), under high dimensionality and a strict evaluation budget, attributed to exploiting block-epsilon-separability of the search space.

cards.heading: Results
cards.question: How did the coordinated system perform relative to its individual member models?
cards.answer: It outperformed every individual member model and existing methods across coding, math, reasoning, and domain-knowledge tasks, generalizing to out-of-distribution tasks and reaching 86.2% on LiveCodeBench.
